Document: Part 62 – Arbitration Claims
Part 2 of 2
==================================================
## Registration in High Court of foreign awards

## 62.20

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.20] (1) Where –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.20] (a) an award is made in proceedings on an arbitration in any part of a British overseas territory or other territory to which Part I of the Foreign Judgments (Reciprocal Enforcement) Act 1933 14 (‘the 1933 Act’) extends;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.20] (b) Part II of the Administration of Justice Act 1920 15 extended to that part immediately before Part I of the 1933 Act was extended to that part; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.20] (c) an award has, under the law in force in the place where it was made, become enforceable in the same manner as a judgment given by a court in that place,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.20] rules 74.1 to 74.7 and 74.9 apply in relation to the award as they apply in relation to a judgment given by the court subject to the modifications in paragraph (2). [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.20] (2) The modifications referred to in paragraph (1) are as follows –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.20] (a) for references to the State of origin are substituted references to the place where the award was made; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.20] (b) the written evidence required by rule 74.4 must state (in addition to the matters required by that rule) that to the best of the information or belief of the maker of the statement the award has, under the law in force in the place where it was made, become enforceable in the same manner as a judgment given by a court in that place. ## Registration of awards under the Arbitration (International Investment Disputes) Act 1966

## 62.21

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (1) In this rule –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (a) ‘the 1966 Act’ means the Arbitration (International Investment Disputes) Act 1966 16 ;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (b) ‘award’ means an award under the Convention;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (c) ‘the Convention’ means the Convention on the settlement of investment disputes between States and nationals of other States which was opened for signature in Washington on 18th March 1965 17 ;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (d) ‘judgment creditor’ means the person seeking recognition or enforcement of an award; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (e) ‘judgment debtor’ means the other party to the award. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (2) Subject to the provisions of this rule, the following provisions of Part 74 apply with such modifications as may be necessary in relation to an award as they apply in relation to a judgment to which Part I of the Foreign Judgments (Reciprocal Enforcement) Act 1933 18 applies –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (a) rule 74.1;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (b) rule 74.3;

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (c) rule 74.4(1), (2)(a) to (d), and (4);

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (d) rule 74.6 (except paragraph (3)(c) to (e)); and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (e) rule 74.9(3). [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (3) An application to have an award registered in the High Court under section 1 of the 1966 Act 19 must be made in accordance with the Part 8 procedure. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (4) The written evidence required by rule 74.4 in support of an application for registration must –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (a) exhibit the award certified under the Convention instead of the judgment (or a copy of it); and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (b) in addition to stating the matters referred to in rule 74.4(2)(a) to (d) state whether –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (i) at the date of the application the enforcement of the award has been stayed (provisionally or otherwise) under the Convention; and

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (ii) any, and if so what, application has been made under the Convention, which, if granted, might result in a stay of the enforcement of the award. [PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (5) Where, on granting permission to register an award or an application made by the judgment debtor after an award has been registered, the court considers –

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (a) that the enforcement of the award has been stayed (whether provisionally or otherwise) under the Convention; or

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] (b) that an application has been made under the Convention which, if granted, might result in a stay of the enforcement of the award,

[PART 62 – ARBITRATION CLAIMS > 62.21] the court may stay the enforcement of the award for such time as it considers appropriate. ## Footnotes
